question: Which of the following is a primary function of the District Courts in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Advising the President of India
Hearing appeals from lower courts within the district
Settling disputes between Union and State governments
Issuing writs to enforce fundamental rights (without High Court)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hearing appeals from lower courts within the district

Explanation:
The District Court in India is the highest judicial body at the district level. Its primary function is to hear appeals from lower courts (like Munsif, Civil Judge) within the district and deliver judgments. It also handles civil and criminal cases. The other options are incorrect: Advising the President is the function of the Supreme Court; disputes between Union and State governments are settled by the Supreme Court; issuing writs for fundamental rights is mainly the power of the High Court and Supreme Court. District Courts are established under Article 233 of the Constitution of India.

☛ Under which Article is the District Court established? → Article 233
☛ Through which power does the High Court supervise District Courts? → Superintendence power (Article 227)
☛ Who appoints the District Judge? → Governor, in consultation with the High Court
☛ At what level are cases heard in the District Court? → Appellate and original level
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भारत में जिला न्यायालयों का प्राथमिक कार्य है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति को सलाह देना
जिले के भीतर निचली अदालतों से अपील सुनना
संघ और राज्य सरकारों के बीच विवादों का निपटारा करना
मौलिक अधिकारों को लागू करने के लिए रिट जारी करना (उच्च न्यायालय के बिना)
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है जिले के भीतर निचली अदालतों से अपील सुनना

Explanation:
भारत में जिला न्यायालय जिला स्तर पर सर्वोच्च न्यायिक निकाय है। इसका प्राथमिक कार्य जिले के भीतर निचली अदालतों (जैसे मुंसिफ, सिविल जज) से आने वाली अपीलों को सुनना और निर्णय देना है। यह सिविल और आपराधिक मामलों की सुनवाई भी करता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं: राष्ट्रपति को सलाह देना सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का कार्य है; संघ और राज्य के बीच विवादों का निपटारा सर्वोच्च न्यायालय करता है; रिट जारी करना मुख्यतः उच्च न्यायालय और सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का अधिकार है। जिला न्यायालय की स्थापना भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 233 के तहत की जाती है।

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the impeachment procedure of the President?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 61
Article 66
Article 52
Article 54
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 61

Explanation:
Article 61 of the Indian Constitution deals with the impeachment of the President. The President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution. The process begins in either House of Parliament with a charge preferred after 14 days' notice. The resolution must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of that House. It is then sent to the other House, which investigates the charge. If the other House also passes the resolution by a two-thirds majority, the President is removed from office. Article 52 provides for the office of President, while Article 54 and 66 deal with the election of President and Vice-President respectively.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Ground for impeachment of President → Violation of Constitution
☛ Majority required for impeachment resolution → Two-thirds of total membership
☛ House initiating impeachment → Any House of Parliament
☛ Article dealing with President's impeachment → Article 61
☛ Article for removal of Vice-President → Article 67
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद राष्ट्रपति की महाभियोग प्रक्रिया से संबंधित है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 61
अनुच्छेद 66
अनुच्छेद 52
अनुच्छेद 54
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 61

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 61 राष्ट्रपति के महाभियोग (Impeachment) की प्रक्रिया निर्धारित करता है। राष्ट्रपति पर संविधान का उल्लंघन करने का आरोप लगाकर महाभियोग चलाया जा सकता है। यह प्रक्रिया संसद के किसी भी सदन में शुरू होती है, जिसमें आरोप प्रस्ताव को 14 दिनों की पूर्व सूचना के बाद पेश किया जाता है। प्रस्ताव को उस सदन के कुल सदस्यों के 2/3 बहुमत से पारित होना आवश्यक है। इसके बाद दूसरा सदन इसकी जांच करता है और यदि वह भी 2/3 बहुमत से प्रस्ताव पारित करता है, तो राष्ट्रपति पद से हटा दिया जाता है। अनुच्छेद 52 राष्ट्रपति पद का प्रावधान करता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 54 और 66 क्रमशः राष्ट्रपति और उपराष्ट्रपति के चुनाव से संबंधित हैं।

question: What has the Supreme Court of India ruled regarding the independence of tribunals?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Tribunals must be headed by sitting High Court judges to ensure credibility.
Tribunals are executive bodies and need not be independent of the executive.
Tribunals, being quasi-judicial bodies, must be independent of the executive, just like regular courts.
Tribunals can be managed by the subject-matter ministry to improve efficiency.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tribunals, being quasi-judicial bodies, must be independent of the executive, just like regular courts.

Explanation:
The Supreme Court of India has clarified that tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies and must be independent of the executive, just like regular courts. This ruling strengthens the principle of judicial independence, which is a cornerstone of democracy. To ensure the independence of tribunals, the Court held that the appointment of judicial members requires the recommendation of the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court. Additionally, decisions of tribunals are subject to judicial review by the High Court and the Supreme Court. Thus, keeping tribunals free from executive control is essential in the interest of justice.

☛ Whose recommendation is required for appointing judicial members in tribunals? → Chief Justice of the High Court
☛ Who can review the decisions of tribunals? → High Court and Supreme Court
☛ What type of bodies are tribunals? → Quasi-judicial
☛ From which branch of government must tribunals be independent? → Executive
question_hi: भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने न्यायाधिकरणों की स्वतंत्रता के संबंध में क्या फैसला सुनाया है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: न्यायाधिकरणों की विश्वसनीयता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए उनकी अध्यक्षता उच्च न्यायालय के मौजूदा न्यायाधीशों द्वारा की जानी चाहिए।
न्यायाधिकरण कार्यकारी निकाय हैं और इन्हें कार्यपालिका से स्वतंत्र होने की आवश्यकता नहीं है।
न्यायाधिकरण, अर्ध-न्यायिक निकाय होने के नाते, नियमित अदालतों की तरह कार्यपालिका से स्वतंत्र होने चाहिए।
दक्षता में सुधार के लिए न्यायाधिकरणों का प्रबंधन विषय-वस्तु मंत्रालय द्वारा किया जा सकता है।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है न्यायाधिकरण, अर्ध-न्यायिक निकाय होने के नाते, नियमित अदालतों की तरह कार्यपालिका से स्वतंत्र होने चाहिए।

Explanation:
भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने स्पष्ट किया है कि न्यायाधिकरण अर्ध-न्यायिक निकाय हैं और इन्हें कार्यपालिका से स्वतंत्र होना चाहिए, ठीक वैसे ही जैसे नियमित अदालतें होती हैं। यह निर्णय न्यायिक स्वतंत्रता के सिद्धांत को मजबूत करता है, जो लोकतंत्र की आधारशिला है। न्यायाधिकरणों की स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए न्यायालय ने कहा कि इनमें न्यायिक सदस्यों की नियुक्ति में उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश की सिफारिश आवश्यक है। इसके अलावा, न्यायाधिकरणों के निर्णयों की न्यायिक समीक्षा उच्च न्यायालय और सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा की जा सकती है। इस प्रकार, न्यायाधिकरणों को कार्यपालिका के नियंत्रण से मुक्त रखना न्याय के हित में अनिवार्य है।

question: Which of the following is a socio-economic Directive Principle? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Promotion of international peace
Equal pay for equal work
Separation of powers
Independence of the judiciary
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Equal pay for equal work

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) in Part IV of the Indian Constitution aim to establish social and economic justice. Article 39(d) specifically provides for equal pay for equal work for both men and women, which is a socio-economic directive principle. It focuses on eliminating gender-based wage discrimination and ensuring economic fairness. Other options: Promotion of international peace (Article 51) is a global principle, while Separation of powers and Independence of the judiciary are political and constitutional principles, not socio-economic in nature.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Equal pay for equal work → Provided under Article 39(d)
☛ Directive Principles of State Policy → Part IV, Articles 36-51
☛ Promotion of international peace → Article 51
☛ Separation of powers → Inspired by US Constitution, not explicitly in Indian Constitution
☛ Independence of judiciary → Part of constitutional framework, not a DPSP
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक सामाजिक-आर्थिक निर्देशक सिद्धांत है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति को बढ़ावा देना
समान काम के लिए समान वेतन
शक्तियों का पृथक्करण
न्यायपालिका की स्वतंत्रता
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है समान काम के लिए समान वेतन

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य के नीति निर्देशक तत्व (DPSPs) का उल्लेख है। ये तत्व सामाजिक-आर्थिक न्याय स्थापित करने के लिए हैं। अनुच्छेद 39(d) के अनुसार, पुरुषों और महिलाओं दोनों के लिए समान काम के लिए समान वेतन का प्रावधान एक सामाजिक-आर्थिक निर्देशक सिद्धांत है। यह समाज में लैंगिक असमानता को दूर करने और आर्थिक न्याय सुनिश्चित करने पर केंद्रित है। अन्य विकल्प: अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति को बढ़ावा देना (अनुच्छेद 51) एक वैश्विक सिद्धांत है, शक्तियों का पृथक्करण और न्यायपालिका की स्वतंत्रता राजनीतिक और संवैधानिक सिद्धांत हैं, सामाजिक-आर्थिक नहीं।

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: 101st Amendment
106th Amendment
103rd Amendment
97th Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 101st Amendment

Explanation:
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, which came into effect on 1 July 2017. GST subsumed multiple indirect taxes like VAT, service tax, excise duty, etc., into a unified tax system. This amendment added a new Article 246A to the Constitution, empowering both the Centre and States to levy GST. It also established the GST Council, a federal body that decides tax rates and policies. The 101st Amendment was a landmark reform in India's indirect tax structure.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Constitutional Amendment for GST → 101st Amendment (2016)
☛ Date of GST implementation → 1 July 2017
☛ New Article added for GST → 246A
☛ Constitutional body for GST → GST Council
☛ Taxes subsumed under GST → VAT, service tax, excise duty, etc.
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस संवैधानिक संशोधन ने भारत में गुड्स एंड सर्विसेज टैक्स (GST) किया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारत में गुड्स एंड सर्विसेज टैक्स (GST) को 101वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2016 द्वारा लागू किया गया। यह संशोधन 1 जुलाई 2017 से प्रभावी हुआ। GST ने केंद्र और राज्य स्तर पर अप्रत्यक्ष करों जैसे वैट, सेवा कर, उत्पाद शुल्क आदि को समाहित कर एक एकीकृत कर प्रणाली बनाई। इस संशोधन ने संविधान में नए अनुच्छेद 246A जोड़े, जो केंद्र और राज्यों को GST लगाने की शक्ति देते हैं। साथ ही, GST परिषद का गठन किया गया जो कर दरों और नीतियों पर निर्णय लेती है। 101वां संशोधन भारत के अप्रत्यक्ष कर ढांचे में एक बड़ा सुधार था।

question: Who presides over the sessions of the Vidhan Sabha in a State? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Governor of the State
The Chief Minister of the State
The Speaker elected by members
The Deputy Speaker by rotation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Speaker elected by members

Explanation:
According to Article 178 of the Indian Constitution, the Vidhan Sabha elects a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker from among its members. The Speaker presides over the sessions of the Vidhan Sabha. In their absence, the Deputy Speaker presides. The Governor is not a member of the house; they summon the session and deliver the address. The Chief Minister leads the government but does not preside over the house. The Speaker ensures the orderly conduct of business, maintains discipline, and grants members the opportunity to speak. Thus, the sessions of the Vidhan Sabha are presided over by the Speaker elected by its members.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who elects the Vidhan Sabha Speaker? → Members of Vidhan Sabha
☛ Who presides in the absence of Speaker? → Deputy Speaker
☛ When does the Governor address the Vidhan Sabha? → At the start of the session

question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is guaranteed under Article 14 of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Equality before the law
Right to freedom of religion
Prohibition of child labour
Protection of life and personal liberty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Equality before the law

Explanation:
Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees Equality before the law and Equal protection of the laws. This Fundamental Right prevents the State from treating any person unequally before the law. It is available to all persons, not just citizens. Article 14 forms the basis of the Right to Equality and is read along with Articles 15, 16, 17, and 18. However, this right is not absolute; the State can make reasonable classifications, such as in reservation policies. The other options: 'Right to freedom of religion' falls under Article 25, 'Prohibition of child labour' under Article 24, and 'Protection of life and personal liberty' under Article 21.

question: When was the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) enacted to regulate and promote the real estate sector, ensuring transparency and accountability in transactions and protecting the interests of homebuyers? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:
The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) was enacted by the Indian Parliament in the year 2016 to regulate and promote the real estate sector, ensuring transparency, accountability, and protection of homebuyers' interests. It came into effect on 1 May 2017, with 59 out of 68 sections being enforced initially. The remaining sections were implemented later. Under RERA, each state is required to establish a Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA) to register projects, resolve disputes, and monitor compliance. The act imposes penalties on developers for project delays and non-compliance, thereby safeguarding buyers from unfair practices. RERA has significantly improved the trust and efficiency in the real estate market by mandating project registration, quarterly progress reports, and clear title deeds.

question: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following acts was aimed at establishing a federal polity in India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Indian Councils Act, 1892
Rowlatt Act, 1919
Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1858
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1935

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1935 was aimed at establishing a federal polity in India. It ended dyarchy in provinces and introduced provincial autonomy, while proposing a federal structure at the centre. The act created three lists (federal, provincial, and concurrent). Although the federal part was never implemented, this act became the blueprint for the Indian Constitution. It also provided for a federation of British Indian provinces and princely states, though it was never fully realized.

question: The Planning Commission was the nodal body for central planning in India. Who served as the first Chairman of the Planning Commission? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The Planning Commission was established on 15 March 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India to formulate and monitor the implementation of five-year plans for the country's economic development. The Planning Commission remained the nodal body for central planning until its dissolution in 2014, after which the NITI Aayog was constituted to replace it.

question: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that judicial review is a basic feature of the Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Shah Bano case
Shankari Prasad case
Kesavananda Bharati case
Golaknath case
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kesavananda Bharati case

Explanation:
In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), a 13-judge bench of the Supreme Court held that judicial review is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution. This landmark judgment established the basic structure doctrine, which limits Parliament's power to amend the Constitution. According to this doctrine, Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, but it cannot destroy or alter the basic features such as judicial review, federalism, and fundamental rights. The case ensured that the judiciary retains its power to review the constitutional validity of laws. This decision overruled the earlier Golaknath case (1967), which had held that fundamental rights could not be amended. The Kesavananda Bharati case remains a cornerstone of Indian constitutional law.

question: Which of the following is a distinctive feature of a statutory corporation in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: It has no legal existence separate from the government.
It is wholly owned by private shareholders and receives no government funding.
It is created by a special Act, has independent legal status and can be sued.
Its employees are considered government civil servants under normal rules.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Option 3: It is created by a special Act, has independent legal status and can be sued.

Explanation:
The distinctive feature of a statutory corporation in India is that it is established by a special Act passed by the Parliament or state legislature. It has an independent legal status, meaning it can own property, enter into contracts, sue and be sued in its own name, separate from the government. It enjoys financial autonomy, though its capital is wholly provided by the government. Its employees are not government civil servants but are governed by the corporation's own regulations. Other options: Option 1 is incorrect because statutory corporations do have a legal existence separate from the government; Option 2 is wrong because they are not owned by private shareholders, rather by the government; Option 4 is false as employees are not considered government civil servants.

question: Which of the following is an unstatutory and unconstitutional body? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Attorney General of India
NITI Aayog
Central Information Commission
National Human Rights Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is NITI Aayog

Explanation:
NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is an unstatutory and unconstitutional body. It was established on 1 January 2015 through a cabinet resolution of the Government of India, replacing the Planning Commission. It was not created by any Act of Parliament or under any article of the Constitution but came into existence via an executive order. In contrast, the Attorney General of India (Article 76), the Central Information Commission (Right to Information Act 2005), and the National Human Rights Commission (Protection of Human Rights Act 1993) are either constitutional or statutory bodies.

question: Which amendment abolished the privy purse and privileges of the former rulers of princely states? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Thirty-first Amendment Act, 1972
Twenty-Fourth Amendment Act, 1971
Twenty-Sixth Amendment Act, 1971
Twenty-fifth Amendment Act, 1971
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Twenty-Sixth Amendment Act, 1971

Explanation:
The Twenty-Sixth Amendment to the Indian Constitution was enacted in 1971. It abolished the privy purse and privileges granted to former rulers of princely states. The amendment removed Articles 291 and 362 from the Constitution. The privy purse was an annual payment made to former rulers as part of the merger agreements. This move was taken under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's leadership to reinforce the principles of equality and republicanism. After this amendment, former rulers lost all special privileges and became equal to ordinary citizens. The amendment was challenged in the Supreme Court but was upheld.

☛ Articles removed by 26th Amendment → 291 and 362
☛ Basis of privy purse → Merger agreements with princely states
☛ Prime Minister during 26th Amendment → Indira Gandhi
☛ Purpose of abolishing privy purse → Promote equality and secularism

question: Which of the following states come under the Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Mizoram and Manipur
Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh
Nagaland and Meghalaya
Assam and Tripura
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh

Explanation:
The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It applies to states with significant tribal populations. Currently, ten states fall under the Fifth Schedule: Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, and Telangana. Among these, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh are included. States like Mizoram, Manipur, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Assam, and Tripura come under the Sixth Schedule, which provides separate provisions for tribal areas in the northeastern states. The Fifth Schedule ensures special safeguards for Scheduled Tribes through the establishment of Tribes Advisory Councils and the governor's role in regulating laws related to land and resources.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ How many states are under the Fifth Schedule? → Ten
☛ Which Schedule applies to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram? → Sixth Schedule
☛ What body is set up in Fifth Schedule states for tribal welfare? → Tribes Advisory Council
☛ What is the purpose of the Fifth Schedule? → Special provisions for welfare and protection of Scheduled Tribes
☛ Which amendment included Chhattisgarh in the Fifth Schedule? → State Reorganization Act of 2000
